body_md:
This is a sample post used only for the drafting workflow dry run. It is not an article, it carries no legal content, and it is never filed on the live site. A real run refuses any slug that starts with the word sample.

The checks in this file mirror the rules the site publishes in its content brief, version 1: a word range, six required sections, a list of banned phrases, the general disclaimer word for word, a link to the contact page, and a small number of internal links that all exist in the site inventory. When the owner changes the brief in the admin, this file and its fixture are refreshed to match.

A related page for reference is [the practice areas page](/practice-areas), and a second one is [the locations page](/locations).

## What to do after a dry run

When a dry run passes, the next step is for the Blog desk to write a real post from the live brief and push it to a queue branch. The workflow then reads the live brief again, because the site is the authority on its own policy, and refuses the file if it breaks any rule.

Questions about a specific situation belong with a lawyer. To reach the firm, use [the contact page](/contact), which lists the current details.

More background on how the site is organised is on [the blog index](/blog).

The queue branch is one of the things this fixture exists to exercise. When it is wrong, the drafter names the queue branch in its list of problems and stops before anything is written to the site, so the owner can read the message and decide what to change. ## Frequently asked questions

**Is this a real article?** No. It is a fixture for tests.

**Does a dry run create anything?** No. It reads, checks and reports.

**Can a queue file publish a post?** No. The workflow never sends a publish field, and the key has no publish right.

**Why do the headings look odd?** The checker reads each required section as a kind of heading, so the fixture headings use plain reader words that the checker accepts.
